newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Brother-in-law of Cambodian PM shot dead.
newsitem.headline: Brother-in-law of Cambodian PM shot dead.

text.p: The brother-in-law of Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen was shot dead on Tuesday morning in central Phnom Penh, witnesses and officials said.
Keov Savuth, 39, was shot in the chest three times by two unidentified gunmen as he left a restaurant, said a restaurant worker who saw the murder.
Family members said he was shot five times.
Keov Savuth, a police officer who was married to Hun Sen's wife's sister, died soon after arriving at a Phnom Penh hospital, officials said.
A spokesman for Hun Sen, Om Yentieng, said: "This is a political murder," adding that the second prime minister had cancelled his official schedule today.
Om Yentieng said he believed he himself was also under threat. He said Hun Sen had ordered security guards to watch him and any other possible targets for assassination.
"This is not the first time that Hun Sen's family has been targeted," he said, citing the murder of Hun Sen's father-in-law in 1992.
The event brings political tensions in Phnom Penh to a head.

At the weekend, 10 Cambodians who said they had been undercover Khmer Rouge agents accused opposition leader and former finance minister Sam Rainsy of taking secret funds and support from the pariah Maoist movement. Sam Rainsy advocates reconciliation with the Khmer Rouge.
The men, who said they were defecting Khmer Rouge spies from Phnom Penh, met Hun Sen on Saturday.

The self-proclaimed guerrillas said they had given support and funding to an opposition party since co-Premiers Hun Sen and Prince Norodom Ranariddh formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run elections in 1993.
Ranariddh called the men liars and Sam Rainsy said he had been slandered.
Om Yentieng drew a connection between the weekend's controversial events and Tuesday's murder.
"I think it is a political assassination... There were many people angry on Saturday," he said. "The order (to murder) came from inside Cambodia."
An adviser to Ranariddh told Reuters: "The prince has condemned this act very severely on behalf of (his) FUNCINPEC party."
An investigation had begun and three witnesses were being interviewed, officials said.
